source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Reference the testing protocols used to detect the quality issues.
3. Verify the results against the acceptable standards.
4. Identify the contaminants found and compare against safe levels.
5. Record the date, time, and location of the test.
6. Document any deviations from standard procedure that occurred during testing.
7. Notate any immediate actions taken in response to the failed test.
8. Confirm all results with a second sample, to ensure accuracy and repeatability.
9. Consult health authorities or experts if the contaminants pose immediate health risks.
10. Prepare the written report detailing the failed test results and actions taken.
11. Ensure the report is clear and understandable for the public and stakeholders.
12. Submit the report to relevant authorities and post on official communication channels if required.
13. Notify the public through reliable communication channels (e.g. press releases, local news outlets, town hall meetings, social media).
14. Inform water users immediately, either directly or
